project: Conan — v4.5-timeline: hook + skill firing per-terminal split panel (with honest 'considered but not fired' capture)
description: A live, per-terminal-tab Timeline split panel showing hook events, build-loop iterations, skills fired (transcript ground truth), and the genuinely new bit — skills *considered but didn't fire* for each prompt, scored by a small BM25-over-descriptions matcher plus a categorical-reason rule layer. Labelled honestly as a heuristic in the UI (Claude doesn't expose its real skill scoring). The prototype split layout + tab-tethered UX is already on disk (loop/conan-v4.4: TimelineMock.tsx, TerminalPane.tsx split + toggle next to '+'). This loop wires up the four data lanes (3 of which already broadcast over /ws), adds the considered-scorer + a `prompt_consideration` table, replaces the mock with a live Timeline.tsx, and ships per-tab split persistence + ⌘\ shortcut. The Skills HUD tab gains a 'last fired' stamp as a free side-effect of the transcript scan. Source: docs/timeline-prd.md. Decisions (2026-05-28): skills-considered ships as heuristic+transcript (Conan's BM25 + rule layer, labelled 'Heuristic match' in the UI); scope = per active terminal tab (the visual tether IS the binding); Timeline is a vertical split inside the active terminal pane, not a top-level tab. Backend foundations before UI; build stays green at every story.

userStories.title: Timeline read endpoint + normalized TimelineRow envelope
userStories.description: As a Conan user, I want a single chronological read for a session's hook + loop events, so the Timeline UI can backfill on mount without juggling multiple sources.
acceptanceCriteria: GET /api/claude/timeline?session=…&since=…&limit=… returns a flat list of TimelineRow envelopes in descending ts order (newest first), token-gated

TimelineRow is a discriminated union with `kind: 'hook' | 'loop' | 'skill-fired' | 'skill-considered'` and a common `{ts: number}`; hook rows carry {eventId, subtype, title, detail?, payload?}; loop rows carry {subtype: 'iteration'|'pass'|'trail', title, detail?}

Hook rows come from the `event` table filtered by session_id (only stream_type='hook') with payload-derived subtype/title/detail (UserPromptSubmit → 'PROMPT' + truncated prompt; Pre/PostToolUse → 'PRETOOL'/'POSTTOOL' + tool name + first arg; Stop → 'STOP'; Notification → 'NOTIF'; SessionStart/End → 'SESSION')

Loop rows come from progress.txt's recent lines (`readTasks().activity`) filtered to the session's cwd (the session's cwd matches the progress.txt's project — match on substring of the activity text or via the session row's cwd); subtype 'iteration'|'pass'|'trail' derived from the line
skill-fired and skill-considered envelope shapes are defined in this story (carried by US-002/T03) but the endpoint returns [] for those kinds in THIS story
`since` filters strictly greater-than ts; `limit` clamps to [1, 500] with a default 200; an unknown/missing session returns an empty array
A unit test covers the envelope mapping (one fixture row per hook subtype) and the empty/clamp/limit branches
npm test passes all suites
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: Backend foundation. The UI consumes existing {type:'event'} and {type:'tasks'} WS broadcasts for live updates — no new WS plumbing in this story. Anchors: POST /api/claude/events ingest + INSERT INTO event in src/gateway/index.ts (~:140/:189); broadcast({type:'event'}) ~:212; watchTasks + readTasks().activity in src/tasks/index.ts (~:125). Add the new route + envelope in src/timeline/index.ts (new module) wired from src/gateway/index.ts.

userStories.title: Transcript-derived skills-fired feed + Skills tab 'last fired' stamp
userStories.description: As a Conan user, I want to see which skills actually fired in each session and how recently each installed skill was used, so I can spot real usage from the timeline and the Skills tab.
acceptanceCriteria: New src/timeline/transcriptScan.ts reads a session's JSONL (prefer `transcript_path` carried in the latest hook payload; fall back to transcriptPath() from src/transcript/index.ts when missing) and extracts every Skill tool_use block as a {skill, ts, promptEventId} record, where promptEventId is the latest UserPromptSubmit event_id before the Skill's ts

The Timeline read route (US-001) merges these rows into the response as `{kind: 'skill-fired', ts, eventId, skill, promptEventId, detail}` envelopes, in correct chronological order with the hook/loop rows

A live watcher (fs.watch + size-delta tail since last byte offset) emits each new Skill block as a `{type:'skill-fired', payload: TimelineRow}` WS broadcast (kept SEPARATE from {type:'event'} so existing WS consumers don't have to parse the new kind)

GET /api/claude/skills returns a `lastFiredAt: number | null` (epoch ms) on each SkillEntry, computed by scanning recent transcripts (bounded — e.g. the latest N JSONLs touched in the last 30 days) and taking the most recent Skill tool_use timestamp per skill name
The Skills HUD tab (SkillsWidget.tsx) renders a `last fired Xm ago` muted line on each row when lastFiredAt is set, or omits the line when null — never fabricates
A unit test on the JSONL parser covers a real fixture (a real session JSONL with ≥1 Skill block) and asserts skill/ts extraction + the null case
An integration test asserts SkillEntry.lastFiredAt is populated for at least one skill in a fixture session
npm test passes all suites
Typecheck passes
cd ui && npm run build is clean
Verify in browser using automate-browser skill (a session with prior Skill firings shows 'last fired' stamps on Skills tab rows; the Timeline route returns at least one skill-fired row)
userStories.notes: Anchors: transcriptPath() + TranscriptBlock 'tool_use' in src/transcript/index.ts (:27, :47); readSkills/SkillEntry in src/skills/index.ts (:25). The UserPromptSubmit hook payload carries `transcript_path` directly (verified: keys are session_id/transcript_path/cwd/permission_mode/hook_event_name/prompt) — prefer that over re-deriving. SkillEntry already gained `path?: string` post-v4.4. Suggested skills: automate-browser.

userStories.title: Skill-consideration scorer + prompt_consideration table + Stop-time reconciliation
userStories.description: As a Conan user, I want to see which skills were considered for each of my prompts and the heuristic reason each didn't fire, so the most opaque thing about skills (`why didn't X trigger?`) becomes legible. (Labelled honestly as a heuristic — not the model's real internal scoring.)
acceptanceCriteria: New src/skills/match.ts exports scoreSkills(prompt: string, skills: SkillEntry[]): {skill: string; score: number; reason: string}[] — BM25 (k1=1.2, b=0.75) over each skill's description (lower-cased, stop-word-stripped, single-word tokens) vs the prompt; pure function, zero deps

A small categorical-reason rule layer converts (score + cheap regexes) into the human-readable reason: `prompt mentions this skill` (skill name appears in prompt), `UI keyword match` (description contains 'browser'/'verify'/'UI' AND prompt has a UI verb like render/screenshot/click/style), `diagram intent` (description+prompt both reference diagram/chart/flowchart), `strong description match (terms: …)` (score ≥ HIGH), `partial match (terms: …)` (score in [LOW, HIGH)), `no description match (top terms: …)` (otherwise)

A new SQLite table `prompt_consideration (event_id INTEGER, skill TEXT, score REAL, reason TEXT, fired INTEGER DEFAULT 0, created_at INTEGER, PRIMARY KEY (event_id, skill))` is added with idempotent init (no crash on existing DBs)

POST /api/claude/events ingest path: on hook_event_name === 'UserPromptSubmit', scoreSkills(payload.prompt, readSkills(activeCwd())), keep the top 8 by score, INSERT them into prompt_consideration keyed by that event's row id, then broadcast each as `{type:'skill-considered', payload: TimelineRow}` over /ws (separate kind, like skill-fired)

POST /api/claude/events ingest path: on hook_event_name === 'Stop', run the US-002 scanner over the session's JSONL slice since the latest UserPromptSubmit and UPDATE prompt_consideration SET fired=1, reason='<fired_reason>' WHERE event_id=<promptEventId> AND skill IN (<fired skill names>); the matching rows' kind in subsequent reads flips from skill-considered to skill-fired

The Timeline read route (US-001) joins prompt_consideration on the prompt event and emits `{kind: 'skill-considered', ts, eventId, skill, promptEventId, reason, heuristic: true}` rows (heuristic flag always true) for non-fired rows
Unit tests on scoreSkills cover BM25 ranking on a small fixture (prompt + 4 skills) AND each rule's classification (prompt-mentions, UI-keyword, diagram, strong, partial, none)
An integration test posts a fake UserPromptSubmit event, asserts the expected prompt_consideration rows + a `{type:'skill-considered'}` WS broadcast
An integration test posts a Stop event after writing a transcript fixture containing a Skill tool_use; asserts the matching prompt_consideration row flipped fired=1 with the fired reason
npm test passes all suites
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: The novel piece. Honesty constraint: never label this 'why Claude didn't fire X' — only 'heuristic match against the skill's description'. Anchors: ingest path in src/gateway/index.ts (~:140); src/db (table init); src/skills/index.ts (readSkills). Real UserPromptSubmit payload key is `prompt` (verified). Memory mentions a native BM25 search skill in the conan-dashboard codebase (50 docs in 17ms, zero deps) — reuse its stop-word/token list if convenient, but the gateway can roll its own ~50-LOC BM25 with no new dep.

userStories.title: Replace TimelineMock with the live Timeline.tsx (filter chips, live append, honest 'Heuristic' badge, rail-alignment fix)
userStories.description: As a Conan user, I want the Timeline split panel to render real events from my session, so I can actually use it instead of the mockup.
acceptanceCriteria: New ui/src/components/Timeline.tsx (replacing TimelineMock.tsx) takes {token, sessionId, terminalLabel, onClose} props and fetches GET /api/claude/timeline?session=<sessionId>&limit=200 on mount; renders an empty state when there are no rows yet ('No activity yet for this terminal — the timeline fills as Claude Code emits hook events.')

Subscribes to the app /ws and appends incoming `{type:'event'}` (after mapping to a hook TimelineRow), `{type:'skill-considered'}`, and `{type:'skill-fired'}` messages whose session_id matches; ignores other sessions
Loop rows come from existing `{type:'tasks'}` broadcasts (already plumbed) — the latest TasksState.activity lines matching this session's cwd render as 'LOOP' rows interleaved chronologically
Filter chips (All / Hooks / Skills / Loop) are FUNCTIONAL: chips are multi-select (All clears all others), state held locally; filtering hides rows whose kind doesn't match — never tears down data

Each PROMPT row's nested 'Skills considered (N) · fired N' card carries a small 'Heuristic match' badge with a tooltip explaining the data is computed by BM25 description matching, not Claude's actual scoring (anti-fabrication framing per the PRD)
Auto-scroll on new event: ONLY when the user is already at the top (timeline is descending). Otherwise keep their scroll position and show a small `↑ N new` pill that scrolls to top on click
Rail-alignment math fixed: rail centers on the dot column at left-[98px] (px-4 + w-16 + gap-3 + w-3/2). No visible offset between the rail and the dots in any row
TimelineMock.tsx is removed; TerminalPane.tsx's import + per-tab split mounts the new Timeline.tsx passing terminalLabel + the active session id
Mockup footer ('sample data') is gone (replaced by the live data)
Typecheck passes
cd ui && npm run build is clean

Verify in browser using automate-browser skill (open the split for the active tab; row appears live after a hook event; filter chips toggle correctly; 'Heuristic match' badge + tooltip readable; rail aligned to dots; light + dark)
userStories.notes: Depends on US-001 (route), US-002 (skill-fired rows + WS kind), US-003 (skill-considered rows + WS kind). Anchors: ui/src/components/TimelineMock.tsx (the prototype to replace); ui/src/components/TerminalPane.tsx (split toggle next to '+' + per-tab state already plumbed); existing WS subscriber pattern in ui/src/hooks/useTasks.ts / useGateway. userStories.title: Persist per-tab Timeline split state + ⌘\ keyboard shortcut
userStories.description: As a Conan user, I want my Timeline split (open/closed + width) per terminal tab to survive reload, so I don't have to re-open it every time.
acceptanceCriteria: TerminalPane.tsx persists the per-tab timeline split state to sessionStorage under `conan.terms.timeline` (a JSON string-array of tids with the split open) and `conan.terms.timeline.w` (a JSON `{tid: number}` map of widths); writes on every toggle/resize end (debounced)
On mount, restore from sessionStorage: tabs whose tid is in the list reopen with their saved width (defaulting to TIMELINE_DEFAULT_W if no width)
Closing a tab removes the tid from BOTH sessionStorage keys (in addition to the in-memory cleanup already done by closeTerm)
⌘\ (CmdOrCtrl+Backslash) toggles the timeline split for the active tab; the shortcut works whether focus is on the terminal or the HUD; doesn't intercept ⌘\ inside an input/textarea

The native menu (ui/src/lib/appMenu.ts) View submenu gains a 'Split Timeline' item with the ⌘\ accelerator that fires the same action via a window event (conan:toggle-timeline) TerminalPane listens for — consistent with the New/Close Terminal bridge
Toggle button next to '+' continues to work (parity); aria-pressed reflects state
Typecheck passes
cd ui && npm run build is clean
Verify in browser using automate-browser skill (toggle, resize, reload → split state survives; ⌘\ toggles the active tab's split)
userStories.notes: Anchors: TerminalPane.tsx timelineOpen Set + timelineWidth Record + toggleTimelineForActive (already plumbed); persist alongside conan.terms (the existing tid list). Native menu bridge: window CustomEvent pattern in ui/src/lib/appMenu.ts (e.g. conan:new-terminal). Suggested skills: automate-browser.

userStories.title: Extend transcript scanner for TodoWrite + ExitPlanMode → emit Plan rows on the Timeline
userStories.description: As a Conan user, I want the Timeline to show my TodoWrite items and ExitPlanMode plans as PLAN rows, so per-session planning state lives on the same surface as the rest of the session's activity.
acceptanceCriteria: Extend src/timeline/transcriptScan.ts (from US-002) to ALSO extract TodoWrite tool_use blocks as `{kind: 'plan', subtype: 'todo-write', ts, items: [{content: string, activeForm?: string, status: 'pending'|'in_progress'|'completed'}], eventId, promptEventId}` (eventId/promptEventId resolved the same way as the Skill blocks)
Extend the same scanner to extract ExitPlanMode tool_use blocks as `{kind: 'plan', subtype: 'plan-mode', ts, plan: string, eventId, promptEventId}` (plan is the agent's plan text from the tool input)
The Timeline read route (US-001) merges these rows into the response in correct chronological order with hook/loop/skill rows

The live JSONL watcher (from US-002) emits each new TodoWrite/ExitPlanMode block as a `{type: 'plan', payload: TimelineRow}` WS broadcast (separate kind from {type:'event'}, {type:'skill-fired'}, {type:'skill-considered'} so consumers can subscribe granularly)

Unit test on the scanner extension: a JSONL fixture containing one TodoWrite block + one ExitPlanMode block asserts both are extracted with correct shape (items[] with statuses for TodoWrite; plan string for ExitPlanMode); a fixture with NO plan blocks asserts the empty result
Integration test: append a TodoWrite block to a fixture JSONL mid-watch, assert a `{type:'plan'}` WS broadcast lands with the expected payload
npm test passes all suites
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: Depends on US-001 (TimelineRow envelope) and US-002 (transcript scanner + watcher). Anchors: src/timeline/transcriptScan.ts (the scanner US-002 created), the Timeline route + WS broadcast in the gateway. The Plan HUD tab's existing data source (usePlan / readPlanState) is informative for shape — the tool input schemas for TodoWrite/ExitPlanMode are stable. No new tables — TimelineRow plan rows are derived live from the JSONL.
